Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

#include<deque>
#include<vector>
#include<algorithm>
#include<iostream>
using namespace std;

// Definition for a Node.
class Node {
public:
    int val;
    vector<Node*> children;

    Node() {}

    Node(int _val) {
        val = _val;
    }

    Node(int _val, vector<Node*> _children) {
        val = _val;
        children = _children;
    }
};

class Solution {
public:
    vector<int> postorder(Node* root) {
        if (root == nullptr) return {};
        vector<int> res;
        postOrder(root, res);
        
        return res;
    }
    void postOrder(Node* root, vector<int>& res)
    {
        if (root == nullptr) return;
        for (auto child : root->children)
            postOrder(child, res);
        res.push_back(root->val);
    }
};

// Test
int main()
{
    Solution sol;
    
    Node* root = new Node(1);  
    auto child1 = new Node(3);
    auto child11= new Node(5);
    auto child12= new Node(6);
    child1->children.push_back(child11);
    child1->children.push_back(child12);
    root->children.push_back(child1);

    auto child2 = new Node(2);
    auto child3 = new Node(4);
    root->children.push_back(child2);     
    root->children.push_back(child3); 
    
    vector<int> res = sol.postorder(root);
    for (auto num : res)
        cout << num << endl;    

    return 0;
}
